title: Additional OA Reasoning Formats
relevance: Campus OAs test set syllogistic Venn reading, courses of action, assertion-reason links, arrangement machines, eligibility rules, and quantity comparison under fixed option formats.
company_notes: PrepInsta cites Input/Output and Decision Making among company OA formats for AMCAT, Infosys, and TCS.

phases.goal: Establish the fixed conventions for each OA reasoning format and what the candidate must decide.

must_hit.point: Logical Venn: given three categories and four diagrams, judge whether sets are disjoint, partially overlapping (some A are B), or fully contained (all A are B).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the three relationship types and that the task is to pick the diagram that matches them.

must_hit.point: Course of Action: an action follows only if it is a proper, feasible, practical response that reduces or solves the stated problem.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines follow as proper/feasible/practical mitigation, not any related suggestion.

must_hit.point: Assertion-Reason options are exactly: both true and R explains A; both true but R does not explain A; A true R false; A false R true.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the four (a)–(d) truth/explanation outcomes without inventing extra options.

must_hit.point: Input–Output machine: deduce a fixed rule by comparing Input→Step I→Step II… then apply that exact rule to a new input.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Emphasizes step-to-step rule discovery then transfer to a fresh string.

must_hit.point: Eligibility: decide Selected, Rejected, or Referred strictly from stated criteria plus stated exceptions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the three statuses and that exceptions only apply as written.

must_hit.point: Quantitative Comparison: compute/deduce Quantity I and II, then choose among I>II, I<II, I≥II, I≤II, or equal/cannot determine.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recalls the five standard comparison choices.

probes: What is the decision task in each of: Venn diagrams, course of action, assertion-reason, machine I/O, eligibility, and quantity comparison?

hints.1: Name each format’s input and what you must output.
hints.2: Venn = set relation; CoA = follows or not; A&R = truth plus explanation; machine = rule from steps; eligibility = select/reject/refer; QC = compare two quantities.
hints.3: Quote the follow definition for CoA and the four A&R options; for the others, state diagram choice, rule transfer, status from criteria, and the five QC options.

phases.goal: Show how to evaluate set containment/overlap, check CoA/A&R links, run machine steps, and apply eligibility exceptions.

must_hit.point: Venn containment vs overlap: e.g. all dogs and pets are animals so both sit inside Animal, while Dog and Pet partially overlap; all fathers are men so Father ⊂ Man, and Doctor intersects both and extends outside Man.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives at least one full-containment and one partial-overlap/intersect pattern from the Dog/Animal/Pet or Doctor/Man/Father type examples.

must_hit.point: A&R test: insert “because” between A and R to check whether R explains A, not merely whether both statements are true.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses the because-link test; may cite white clothes/heat reflection as explains, or diamond hardness vs refractive index as does not.

must_hit.point: Machine rule example: alternate moving highest remaining number then earliest alphabetical word to the left of the unprocessed suffix, one element per step; if already correct for that step, skip and bring the next needed element.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes alternating number/word left-placement and the skip-when-already-correct behavior (as in Step III for 64/fall).

must_hit.point: Eligibility walk: check each primary rule; if a failed rule has a matching exception and all other rules hold, refer (e.g. M.Tech ≥65% → GM; deposit ≥ Rs. 25,000 plus bond → HR Head); a failed hard rule with no exception rejects even if another exception would apply.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks primary checks then exception routing, including that test-fail without exception rejects despite deposit exception.

probes: Walk through how the arrangement machine decides what moves on each step, and how eligibility exceptions change Selected vs Referred vs Rejected.

hints.1: Compare consecutive machine steps; for eligibility, tick criteria then exceptions.
hints.2: Machine: one left-side placement per step, alternating max number and earliest word, skip if already placed. Eligibility: fail-with-exception → refer; fail-without-exception → reject.
hints.3: State the 90/base/85/cold… alternating rule, the already-at-front skip for 64 bringing fall, and Rahul rejected on test <70% despite deposit exception (B).

phases.goal: Separate valid follow/explain/refer outcomes from extreme, non-explanatory, or irreversible cases.

must_hit.point: Course of Action: measured relief or root-cause enforcement follows; forced mass migration, total highway vehicle bans, or shutting a division after one bad quarter do not.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts I-follows drought relief / speed cameras / market research against extreme II or I actions that do not follow.

must_hit.point: Both A and R true is not enough: R may be true yet fail to explain A (diamond cuts glass from hardness, not high refractive index).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States option (b) case where R is factually true but not the cause of A.

must_hit.point: Machine extraction to the front is not reversible, so original Input cannot be recovered from a later Step (e.g. from Step II).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says prior positions of extracted elements are unknown → cannot be determined.

probes: When does a true Reason still fail, and when does a suggested action fail to follow?
Why can’t you recover the original machine Input from Step II?

hints.1: Ask whether the action is proportionate and whether R causes A.
hints.2: CoA fails on extremes/secondary harm; A&R (b) fails the because-link; machine front-extraction loses prior order.
hints.3: Cite drought I vs forced migration II; diamond refractive index vs hardness; Step II → original Input cannot be determined.

phases.goal: Apply the formats to concrete items and produce the keyed answers with supporting checks.

must_hit.point: Venn answers: Dog/Animal/Pet → large Animal with two smaller overlapping circles; Doctor/Man/Father and Table/Furniture/Wood → one circle inside another with a third intersecting both.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives those three diagram choices with the containment/overlap rationale.

must_hit.point: For Input 64 toll 22 fall 38 ask 75 mass: Step III is 75 ask 64 fall toll 22 38 mass; arrangement completes in 6 steps.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States Step III string (b) and total steps 6.

must_hit.point: Eligibility: Amit (all primary met) Selected; Priya (B.Tech 55% but M.Tech 68% and otherwise OK) Refer to GM; Rahul (test 65%, no exception for rule 3) Rejected.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Assigns Selected / Refer to GM / Rejected with the failing or exception rule named.

must_hit.point: QC: roots 6 or 7 vs 8 or 9 ⇒ I<II; first 50 even and first 51 odd averages both 51 ⇒ equal; circle area 154 vs square 121 ⇒ I>II; A’s age 20 equals Quantity II 20.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the four comparison outcomes using only those figures from the file.

probes: Solve the Dog/Animal/Pet Venn, the 64…mass Step III and step count, Amit/Priya/Rahul status, and one Quantity I vs II comparison.

hints.1: Apply containment first, then overlap; for machine, move one element per step.
hints.2: Eligibility: check 60%/21–30/70%/Rs. 50,000 then exceptions (A)/(B). QC: solve or average then pick the option letter.
hints.3: Dog/Pet inside Animal overlapping; Step III 75 ask 64 fall toll 22 38 mass in 6 steps; Amit Selected, Priya GM, Rahul Rejected; e.g. 154>121 or ages both 20.

tradeoffs.topic: Practical course of action vs extreme overreaction
tradeoffs.strong_answer: An action follows only if it is proper, feasible, and practical and reduces the problem; extremes that ignore rights, destroy utility, or overreact to a minor/single-period issue do not follow (e.g. drought relief yes / forced migration no; speed cameras yes / ban all private vehicles no; market research yes / shut smartphone division after one quarter no).

tradeoffs.topic: Reason true vs Reason explains Assertion
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Both A and R can be true while R still fails to explain A; insert because between them—white clothes comfort because they are bad absorbers and good reflectors of heat (explains), but diamond’s high refractive index does not explain cutting glass (hardness does).

tradeoffs.topic: Selected vs Referred vs Rejected under eligibility exceptions
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Meet all primary criteria → Selected; fail a rule that has a matching exception and meet all else → Refer (M.Tech ≥65% → GM; ≥ Rs. 25,000 plus bond → HR Head); fail a hard rule with no exception → Rejected even if another exception would have applied.

tradeoffs.topic: Forward machine arrangement vs recovering prior Input
tradeoffs.strong_answer: You can apply the deduced left-extraction rule forward to new inputs, but because elements are pulled from unknown prior positions, a later Step does not determine the original Input.

gotchas.trap: Treating any related or partial response as a course of action that follows.
gotchas.correction: It does not follow if it only partly addresses the issue while ignoring the main problem, creates a larger secondary problem, or is an extreme overreaction to a minor issue.

gotchas.trap: Choosing “both true and R explains A” whenever both statements sound true.
gotchas.correction: For option (b), R can be factually correct alone yet fail to explain A—always insert because between A and R.

gotchas.trap: Asserting atmospheric pressure is higher at higher altitudes to explain lower boiling point.
gotchas.correction: A is true but R is false: atmospheric pressure decreases at higher altitudes, which is why the boiling point drops.

gotchas.trap: Saying silver is unused for domestic wires because it is a bad conductor.
gotchas.correction: A is true (cost; copper/aluminum used) but R is false—silver is the best metallic conductor of electricity.

gotchas.trap: Assuming the original machine Input can be reconstructed from a later Step.
gotchas.correction: Front-extraction is not reversible; prior locations are unknown, so the Input cannot be determined.

gotchas.trap: Referring a candidate who fails a hard criterion just because they qualify for a different exception.
gotchas.correction: No exception for the failed rule means immediate Rejected; deposit exception (B) cannot rescue a failed online-test rule.

gotchas.trap: Forcing a move every step even when the needed element is already at the front of the unprocessed suffix.
gotchas.correction: If it is already in the correct position for that step, take no action on it and bring the next required element instead.
